cases.command: head -c 200000 /dev/zero | head -c 1 >/dev/null; echo "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; head -c 40000 /dev/zero | head -c 1 >/dev/null; echo "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; cat /dev/zero | head -c 1 >/dev/null; echo "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"

( cat /missing /dev/zero | head -c 1 >/dev/null; echo "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; { cat /missing /dev/zero; echo "st=$?" >&2; } | head -c 1 >/dev/null; f() { cat /dev/zero; }; f | head -c 1 >/dev/null; echo "${PIPESTATUS[*]}" )

expect.stderr:
cat: /missing: No such file or directory
cat: /missing: No such file or directory
st=141

cases.note: Divergence: GNU bash 5.2.37 prints "141 0\n": seq keeps writing past the 64 KiB pipe buffer after head exits and dies of SIGPIPE. Mirage pulls a writer's next chunk only once the reader took the last, so a lazy source never fetches another page for a reader that is gone; a writer stopped between its writes keeps its own status, and only a write the closed pipe cuts short is SIGPIPE.

cases.command: head -n 1 /dev/zero | head -c 1 >/dev/null; echo "${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; head -c 200000 /dev/zero | cat -n | head -c 1 >/dev/null; echo "${PIPESTATUS[1]} ${PIPESTATUS[2]}"; head -c 40000 /dev/zero | cat -n | head -c 1 >/dev/null; echo "${PIPESTATUS[1]} ${PIPESTATUS[2]}"
